output.headline: Blackstone has bought three Health IT companies and runs an open platform in the sub-sector, making the $300M target a natural add-on.
output.differentiator: Longest deal record on the priority list at 25 deals. Among the sponsors listed, it pays the highest median multiple (17.1x), and its $342M median deal is close to the target's size.
output.why_them: Add-on to its open Health IT platform; size fit

acquirer_overview.title: Large-cap sponsor with a 25-deal, ten-year record
points: 25 deals from 2015 to 2024, of which 22 closed (88%); 23 of 25 were control deals rather than minority stakes [T:record, K:closed_share, K:control_share].
Median deal of $342M, in a range from $10M to $14,354M; 11 of 25 deals sit in the $150M-$600M size band [T:record, K:size_band].
Private Equity segment holds $416.4 billion of Total Assets Under Management as of December 31, 2025 [P:1].

strategic_fit_thesis.title: An add-on to an open Health IT platform, backed by sub-sector precedent
points: Three past deals in the target's own sub-sector, and an open platform there makes the target an add-on rather than a new bet [T:record, A:angles].
Platform Build is a stated motive in 9 of 25 deals, consistent with buying onto an existing platform [M:platform_build].
Past deal count is a modest factor for it; deal size and region fit are slight factors [S:activity, S:not_smaller, S:geo_fit].

precedent_activity.title: Three Health IT deals at 20.2x to 23.5x, all smaller than the target
points: Nexus Clinical Analytics: $71M bolt-on in 2020 at 23.5x EV/EBITDA, the closest add-on precedent [D:MA-2020-0384].
Standard Revenue Cycle ($26M leveraged buyout, 2022, 20.2x) and Lake Clinical Analytics ($21M recapitalization, 2017, 21.1x) [D:MA-2022-0080, D:MA-2017-0305].
Neighbouring sector at scale: Sterling Revenue Cycle, a $458M bolt-on in 2023 at 16.2x [D:MA-2023-0378].

valuation_context.title: Median of comparables is defensible, with headroom up to $356M
points: 13 comparable deals: 19.4x at the lower quartile, 21.4x median, 23.3x at the upper quartile [V:comps].
Margin of 25.0% is above the comparables' median of 22.2% but not in their top quarter, so the 50th percentile anchors; its own median paid is 17.1x [V:comps].
At 5.0x leverage, IRR at the ask is 25.3% against a 20% target; maximum price is $356M on a $239M equity cheque [V:lbo].

risk_flags.title: Thin Health IT focus
risk_flags.concern: Only 3 of 25 deals are in Health IT, and its home sub-sector is Health Insurance [T:record, B:buyer].
risk_flags.mitigant: Its three Health IT deals priced at 20.2x to 23.5x, and the open platform gives an add-on route [D:MA-2020-0384, A:angles].
risk_flags.reality: Sub-sector record is real but small; all three deals were well below the target's size [D:MA-2022-0080, D:MA-2017-0305].

risk_flags.title: Price discipline versus comparables
risk_flags.concern: Its median paid of 17.1x is below the comparables' lower quartile of 19.4x [V:comps].
risk_flags.mitigant: IRR at the ask is 25.3% against a 20% target, with a maximum price of $356M [V:lbo].
risk_flags.reality: It would need to pay above its usual level, but the returns math allows it [V:comps, V:lbo].

risk_flags.title: Auction experience and strategic rivals
risk_flags.concern: Being used to competitive auctions counts slightly against it, and one 2024 deal was withdrawn [S:bidder_exp, D:MA-2024-0347].
risk_flags.reality: Execution is strong, but strategics on the priority list have paid higher median multiples [S:bidder_exp, K:closed_share].

conviction.rationale: Three deals in the target's own sub-sector, an open platform offering the add-on route, and position 2 on the priority list of 10 support the call [T:record, A:angles, R:rank].
